Read as a request for city-and-country ridings as a design (direction). Same 'regional approach' language as the Cardston-area letters 0677, 0680, 0683.

quote: I would like to encourage the Boundary Commission to keep what was proposed, the 2 ridings for East & West Lethbridge to avoid competing interests and priorities for Elected Officials.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Argues that 'competing priorities can arise in a combined rural and urban electoral boundary'.

quote: I would like to support the Commission's approach to opt out of pursuing a hybrid electoral district for Lethbridge. I truly believe that combining urban and rural communities in these ridings does not lead to effective representation.
note: Lethbridge-East resident, university student. 'I hope the recommendations from this report will be maintained.'

quote: Dividing the Lethbridge riding into 4 is ineffective and designed to shore up support for the UCP. Leave the riding as as they are.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Whole message. 'as as' is in the original.

quote: Do not split Lethbridge into 4 districts. This will weaken Lethbridge and not accurately represent our needs.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Whole message. Keeping the two city ridings is implied, not stated: direction.

quote: I suspect it be an attempt to silence the more progressive voting areas by including more rural in urban ridings.
note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge, AB and '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). 'The proposal' she finds 'abhorrent' is adding rural areas to urban ridings, which the interim map did not do in Lethbridge; read as the four-way hybrid idea. Want inferred from the rejection. A stricter reader could code mention only. Hard case.

quote: Boundaries should stay the same. We don't need American gerrymandering in Canada.
note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge and '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). 'Stay the same' is two city ridings under both the map in force and the interim map; whether she also objects to the interim's small change to the internal line is not clear.

quote: I would like to express my support for the decision to maintain two electoral ridings in the city of Lethbridge rather than amalgamating sections of the City with the surrounding rural ridings.
note: Lethbridge-West resident, former school board chair. 'The proposal to fracture the southern ridings and create 4 urban/rural blended ridings would not have met the needs of the residents of southwestern Alberta.'

quote: Electoral boundaries should not be moved
note: Whole message is these six words (under the 8-word minimum; nothing more to quote). Form header: Lethbridge, current Lethbridge-West, about '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). Read as: keep the Lethbridge-West boundaries, hence a city riding. Could equally be an objection to the interim shift of the line between the two city ridings. A stricter reader would code mention only.

quote: The current proposal to split the two Lethbridge ridings into four ridings that meld urban and rural constituencies will serve neither well.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Treats the four-way split as the 'current proposal' (it is not on the interim map). Keeping two city ridings is implied by the rejection: direction.

quote: 72 -Lethbridge-Livingstone-Macleod […] Forecast Population: 52,000
note: from map. 198-page submission by two private citizens with a province-wide alternative map. PDF pages 70 and 142 to 145 opened and read by eye: the map draws four ridings meeting at the city, labelled 72 Lethbridge-Livingstone-Macleod, 73 Lethbridge-North West, 74 Lethbridge-Taber-Warner and 75 Lethbridge-Cardston, and no city-only Lethbridge riding. The text never names Lethbridge; it argues in general that 'Hybrid division that combines cities with nearby rural areas would reduce urban bias' (p. 69). Quote is the map caption (short by necessity). Read in full: text pp. 65-69 and 161-167; the remaining pages are maps and tables, searched for Lethbridge and checked (historical maps and 2017 tables only).

quote: An electoral district that combines parts of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would reflect both regional realities and the intent of the Electoral Boundaries Commission Act.
note: Cardston resident, about interim Cardston-Taber-Warner. Member of the family of Cardston-area round 2 letters with the same argument, statute citations and list of places in varied wording (EBC-2025-2-0677, 0680, 0683, 0788, 0794, 0797, 0808): campaign. Describes one district, in effect the south-west quarter of the four-way plan, and says nothing of the rest of the city: direction; a strict reader could code L3.

quote: A district that links portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would align closely with how people in southern Alberta live, work, and interact
note: Hill Spring resident, about interim Cardston-Taber-Warner. Member of the family of Cardston-area round 2 letters with the same argument, statute citations and list of places in varied wording (EBC-2025-2-0677, 0680, 0683, 0788, 0794, 0797, 0808): campaign. Describes one district, in effect the south-west quarter of the four-way plan, and says nothing of the rest of the city: direction; a strict reader could code L3.

quote: An electoral district that includes parts of Lethbridge alongside the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would accurately reflect both the realities of daily life in southern Alberta
note: Cardston resident, about interim Cardston-Taber-Warner. Member of the family of Cardston-area round 2 letters with the same argument, statute citations and list of places in varied wording (EBC-2025-2-0677, 0680, 0683, 0788, 0794, 0797, 0808): campaign. Describes one district, in effect the south-west quarter of the four-way plan, and says nothing of the rest of the city: direction; a strict reader could code L3.

quote: The most troubling comment on PAGE 69 was because Lethbridge got two ridings, Medicine Hat can’t get at least one.
note: Former Speaker, Medicine Hat; asks for a city-only Medicine Hat riding. Lethbridge is the comparison ('Lethbridge has two urban'); he objects to the interim report's trade-off between the two cities but asks nothing about Lethbridge (rule 6). The letter appears twice in the record (webform text pp. 7-9, attachment pp. 10-14).

quote: An electoral district that brings together portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond and Stirling would meaningfully reflect the realities of life in southern Alberta
note: Cardston resident (Joseph Schow), about interim Cardston-Taber-Warner. Member of the family of Cardston-area round 2 letters with the same argument, statute citations and list of places in varied wording (EBC-2025-2-0677, 0680, 0683, 0788, 0794, 0797, 0808): campaign. Describes one district, in effect the south-west quarter of the four-way plan, and says nothing of the rest of the city: direction; a strict reader could code L3.

quote: I am a rural resident but am very much affected by decisions that effect Lethbridge. Lethbridge is the hub for the rural surrounding.
note: Enchant resident; header lists Cardston-Siksika, Lethbridge-West, Livingstone-Macleod and Lethbridge-East. Describes his dependence on Lethbridge, which leans toward shared ridings, but makes no request. Narrow code (rule 17): mention, no want.

quote: Please leave the guidelines as they are in Lethbridge
note: Whole message. Lethbridge-West resident. 'Guidelines' read as boundaries; 'as they are' is two city ridings under both the map in force and the interim map.

quote: Division is not necessary.
note: Whole message is these four words. Form header: Lethbridge, about '69 - Lethbridge-East'. Probably means the city need not be divided (the four-way idea), but 'division' could also mean the electoral division or the redrawn line. Narrow code (rule 17): mention, no want. Hard case.

quote: I urge the Commission to consider hybrid urban-rural ridings for more effective representation.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Calls the interim changes to the two city ridings a missed opportunity; 'Fair representation suggests Lethbridge would benefit from reconfigured boundaries, such as hybrid urban-rural ridings.' No particulars: direction. (Codebook example 13.)

quote: I am in favour of the quad-Lethbridge riding boundaries.
note: MLA Taber-Warner (also HANSARD-R2-T48-011).

quote: I am in agreement with Lethbridge remaining two urban ridings with some boundary adjustments due to population shifts within the city. I wish to remain in an urban riding.
note: Lethbridge-West resident whose address moves to Lethbridge-East under the interim map; accepts that.

quote: People in Taber are certainly more associated with businesses and activities along the highway 3 corridor specifically between Taber and Lethbridge.
note: Taber resident: keep Taber-Warner with Coaldale, do not restore Cardston-Taber-Warner. Lethbridge named as the end of the corridor; nothing said about sharing a riding with the city (rule 8).

quote: I would respectfully ask you to reconsider a hybrid model that incorporates part of Lethbridge with communities to the East / South East down the Agri Food Corridor that extends down Highway 3.
note: Taber resident. Asks the commission to take up again a hybrid joining part of Lethbridge to the Highway 3 corridor (in effect the Lethbridge-Taber quarter of the four-way plan); says nothing of the rest of the city, so direction, and a strict reader could code L3. Also asks to keep Coaldale with Barnwell, Taber and Bow Island, which reads as a fallback.

MLA Grande Prairie-Wapiti on northern ridings; supports hybrid districts in general and around Edmonton and Calgary (HYBRID-GENERAL G-PRO). Lethbridge never named (screen hit was Crowsnest Pass in the quoted statute). Record of 30,000 characters: read the opening and every passage around hybrid and southern-Alberta keywords, not every line.

quote: I believe that urban electoral needs/concerns are quite different from rural needs. Splitting up urban dilutes this for good representation.
note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge and '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). Argues against splitting up the urban riding and mixing it with rural needs; want inferred from that. A stricter reader could treat it as HYBRID-GENERAL only.

quote: If anything divide the two Lethbridge constituencies into at least three and that would even out populations for representation.
note: Taber resident, mainly asking that Coaldale stay with Taber-Warner. Adds that Lethbridge should have 'at least three' constituencies to even out populations. Does not say the three would take in country, so L9 rather than L3 or L2; the context (a rural writer calling Lethbridge 'our major hub') leans toward shared ridings. Hard case, like EBC-2025-1-0151.

quote: while there is a natural economic link toward Lethbridge, the impact of that city’s urban and surrounding interests differ markedly from those of our rural communities, and I am strongly opposed to extending the boundary in that direction
note: High River resident (same person as EBC-2025-1-0061) defending the north-south Livingstone-Macleod against the interim east-west ridings. Rural side of the question: his riding should not reach toward Lethbridge. Says nothing of how the city is divided, so L1 only at direction.

quote: As the Board of Trustees for Palliser School Division, we serve a broad and diverse region surrounding Lethbridge, including rural communities, towns, villages, and Hutterite colonies.
note: Palliser School Division board. Approves the interim proposals for the rural region around Lethbridge because the division 'would continue to engage with two MLAs'. The city's own ridings are not discussed and nothing is said about joining city and country; a commissioner later characterised this letter as support for two urban Lethbridge MLAs (HANSARD-R2-T48-002), which the text does not say. Narrow code (rules 8 and 17): mention, no want. Hard case.

MLA Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock on northern ridings; the attached letter is the same text as EBC-2025-2-0978 (campaign). Supports hybrid districts in general (HYBRID-GENERAL G-PRO). Lethbridge never named (screen hit was Crowsnest Pass in the quoted statute). Record of 32,000 characters: read the opening and every passage around hybrid and southern-Alberta keywords, not every line.

quote: As a mid size city often compare to Lethbridge, Grand Prairie, etc Medicine deserves to have an elected representative focused on the urban concerns of the city.
note: Medicine Hat resident asking for a city-focused Medicine Hat riding. Lethbridge only a comparison (rule 6).

quote: I don't see any valid reason to change the Lethbridge electoral boundaries.
note: Whole message. Lethbridge-East resident; header ticks 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. Keeping the Lethbridge boundaries is two city ridings under both the map in force and the interim map; whether he also objects to the interim's small internal change is not clear.

quote: at least one fully urban riding, as is afforded to other mid-size cities such as Grande Prairie, Lethbridge, Red Deer, and St. Albert
note: Former Medicine Hat councillor asking for a fully urban Medicine Hat riding. Lethbridge only a comparison (rule 6).

quote: 75 LETHBRIDGE-FORT
note: from map. Canmore resident asking for a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass riding; the text never names Lethbridge. PDF page 4 opened and read by eye: the attached map (a photograph of a screen, titled 'NEW: 64 EASTERN SLOPES') labels the neighbouring ridings '75 LETHBRIDGE-FORT MACLEOD' and '74 LETHBRIDGE-CARDSTON', so it was drawn on a base map that divides Lethbridge among hybrid ridings. The writer asks nothing about Lethbridge: mention, no want. Quote is the OCR of the map label (short by necessity). Text mirrors EBC-2025-2-0442 closely: campaign.
Canmore resident asking for a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass riding. Lethbridge never named.

quote: I am very happy with the Alberta Electoral Boundaries Commission's interim report and the recommendation to not divide Lethbridge into rural-urban constituencies.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Approval of the refusal to divide the city taken as words of rejection of the four-way plan.

quote: I am aware of a proposal to divide and hybridize these electoral districts into multiple new urban/rural districts, and I am emphatically opposed to that suggestion.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Supports the interim's minimal adjustment of Lethbridge East and Lethbridge West.

quote: I appreciate that my urban riding remain urban. I do not support hybridizing my riding with rural areas.
note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge and '69 - Lethbridge-East' (rule 2).

quote: Coaldale is closely integrated into the Highway 3 corridor that links our town with Lethbridge, Taber, and the surrounding rural municipalities.
note: Coaldale resident: keep Coaldale in Taber-Warner. Describes Coaldale's ties to Lethbridge at length but does not say Coaldale should, or should not, share a riding with part of the city (rule 8): mention, no want.

quote: Thank you again for not carving up Lethbridge and tacking us onto rural areas.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. 'I agree with your interim report. Thank you for giving thoughtful decision making to keeping Lethbridge urban.'

quote: the Lethbridge electorate as a community of interest is quite distinct from our surrounding rural neighbours and that proper representation would not be served for either electorate by dividing Lethbridge up further
note: Lethbridge resident moved from West to East by the interim map; agrees with the interim change to the two city ridings.

quote: I do not support the notion that Lethbridge should be divided into three or four blended rural-urban style ridings.
note: Geography professor (same person as EBC-2025-1-0135). Also objects to the interim line between the two city ridings (wants 13th Street kept); that is inside L1.
